mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate decline below 5.5% signals labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when UNRATE < 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3-month moving averages signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through joint momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when both proxies exceed 3m_MA or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 1% MoM signals manufacturing resilience, supporting profit margins and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods identified as late-cycle expansion (GDP > 3% and UNRATE < 5%).

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth (RSAFS) above 0.3% MoM indicates sustained consumer spending, driving short-term equity returns over 5 trading days without regime constraints.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no positive bias (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS > 0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeding 2.5% triggers expectations of monetary tightening, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations for negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (annualized).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) and unemployment decline (UNRATE < 0.3% MoM) signal labor market tightness, increasing consumer income and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE < 0.3% MoM decline
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when both conditions hold or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.0% and rising for 3 months defines a monetary tightening cycle, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months.
